high.title: Peso Up on Yen Intervention, Middle East Peace Deal Hopes
high.summary: The Philippine Peso surged 31 centavos to close at P60.93 per dollar on Monday — its best close in over six weeks — driven by two key catalysts: coordinated USD/JPY intervention by Japanese and U.S. regulators that strengthened the yen broadly, and renewed optimism around a Middle East peace deal reducing geopolitical risk premiums. The yen's recovery exerted softening pressure on the broader U.S. dollar index, providing relief to regional EM currencies including the PHP. The return to sub-P61 territory is technically significant as it signals potential momentum toward the psychologically critical P60 support level. For FX traders, the key question is whether this move is sustained or merely a short-term relief rally. Watch for: (1) durability of the Iran/Middle East de-escalation narrative, (2) whether yen intervention holds USD/JPY in check, and (3) any BSP commentary on the FX move. Bond investors should note that a firmer peso reduces imported inflation pressures, which could reinforce the case for BSP easing later in 2026.

high.title: Peso to Stay Above P60 Until 2027 on Dollar's Strength, Weak Growth
high.summary: Metrobank's research officer Sophia Therese Bonifacio, in a July 30 commentary, projects the Philippine Peso will remain above the P60:USD level through end-2027, citing persistent domestic and external headwinds keeping the currency structurally weak against the greenback. The forecast points to tight domestic economic conditions and a resilient U.S. dollar environment as primary drivers. Notably, Metrobank acknowledges that potential BSP monetary policy easing — once inflation pressures recede — could add further downward pressure on the PHP by narrowing the interest rate differential with the U.S. This is a critical medium-term signal for fund managers: any BSP rate cut cycle, while supportive of bond prices, may simultaneously weigh on the peso. For bond investors, the outlook implies continued elevated hedging costs for unhedged PHP-denominated positions. FX traders should treat P60 not as a floor but as a resistance level, with the structural bias remaining to the upside (i.e., PHP weakness). Watch for BSP's next policy meeting signals and U.S. Fed guidance as key near-term catalysts that could test or validate this forecast.

high.title: T-Bill Yields Decline on Iran Deal Hopes
high.summary: The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) achieved a full P50 billion award at Monday's T-bill auction, with rates declining across all tenors as improved global risk sentiment — driven by easing U.S.-Iran tensions and falling oil prices — boosted demand for Philippine government securities. Total tenders reached a robust P167.742 billion, more than three times the amount on offer and significantly above the P134.519 billion in bids recorded the prior week, underscoring strong investor appetite. The confluence of lower oil prices (reducing inflation expectations) and a firming peso creates a constructive near-term backdrop for Philippine government bonds. Lower oil prices directly ease imported inflation pressures, which strengthens the case for BSP rate cuts — a key bullish driver for bond prices. The oversubscription ratio of 3.35x signals deep liquidity in the system and confirms that domestic investors are actively positioning for a lower-rate environment. For bond traders, the key risk to this rally is a reversal of the geopolitical de-escalation narrative or an unexpected uptick in Philippine CPI data. Monitor upcoming inflation releases and BTr's next fixed-rate Treasury bond auction for directional confirmation.

high.title: Japan, US Confirm Joint Yen-Buying Intervention, Signal Further Action
high.summary: Japan and the United States have confirmed a rare coordinated yen-buying intervention to arrest the yen's slide to fresh 40-year lows, with both governments signaling readiness to act further if needed. The joint action was framed explicitly around preventing global spillovers — particularly upward pressure on US Treasury yields stemming from a simultaneous sell-off in Japanese government bonds (JGBs).

high.title: Why this matters for PHP/FX traders and bond investors:
BTr Fully Awards Bonds as Rates Decline on Easing Middle East Tensions
high.summary:
The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) achieved a full P30 billion award on reissued 20-year Treasury bonds, drawing exceptionally strong demand as total tenders reached P93.799 billion — more than three times the offer size, implying a bid-to-cover ratio of approximately 3.13x. The key driver was improved risk sentiment stemming from easing Middle East tensions, which pushed global crude oil prices lower and reduced inflation risk premium in the market. Lower oil prices directly ease imported inflation pressures for the Philippines, giving bond investors more confidence that BSP rate cuts remain on the table and that the fiscal inflation outlook is benign. For bond investors, the strong auction outcome signals robust demand at the long end of the curve, with rates moving lower. This is constructive for Philippine government bond (PGB) duration positioning. PHP traders should also note that falling oil prices reduce the current account pressure from energy imports, offering mild support to the peso. Watch for follow-through in secondary market yields and the next BTr auction for confirmation of this bullish bond momentum.

---

high.title: Peso slides back to P61 level on uncertainty over US-Iran talks
high.summary: The Philippine peso weakened sharply on Tuesday, losing 23.5 centavos to close at P61.165/USD — reversing the prior session's gains — as mixed signals from US-Iran peace negotiations dampened risk appetite and drove renewed USD demand. The session opened marginally weaker at P60.95, suggesting the selling pressure built progressively through the day. Adding to peso headwinds, the Japanese yen resumed its decline a day after a coordinated joint intervention temporarily propped it up, signaling broader Asian FX fragility. For PHP traders, the return to the P61 handle is a key psychological and technical level to watch. Geopolitical risk premium tied to the US-Iran situation could keep the peso under pressure in the near term, particularly if talks break down further. The interaction between yen weakness and broader EM FX sentiment also warrants close monitoring, as a weaker yen historically amplifies capital outflow pressures across Asian currencies including the PHP. Traders should watch for any BSP verbal or market intervention signals if the peso approaches P61.50.

high.title: BofA sees BSP ending its tightening cycle in August
high.summary: Bank of America Global Research has flagged a pivotal inflection point for BSP monetary policy: a likely 25 basis point rate hike at the August 27 Monetary Board meeting — contingent on July inflation printing below 7% year-on-year — which would bring the benchmark policy rate to 5% and mark the end of the current tightening cycle. This is a critical signal for both the PHP and the Philippine government bond (PGB) market. If BofA's call proves correct, it implies the front-end of the yield curve could begin to price in a terminal rate of 5%, potentially compressing short-tenor yields and steepening the curve as markets start anticipating eventual easing. For the peso, a definitively hawkish-but-done posture from the BSP could provide short-term support through the rate differential channel, but may remove a key pillar of PHP strength once the market fully prices in the end of hikes. The July CPI print — due before the August 27 meeting — becomes the single most important data release for positioning in PHP rates and the peso. Bond investors should consider duration risk carefully around this juncture, as any upside inflation surprise could push the BSP to hike beyond 5%, repricing the entire curve higher.

high.title: Hot money inflows hit $170M in June
high.summary: Net foreign portfolio investment (FPI) inflows into the Philippines reached $170.12 million in June, extending a second consecutive month of net inflows according to BSP data, though declining from the $232.46 million recorded in May. The sustained net inflow trend is a positive structural signal for the PHP, as portfolio flows represent a meaningful source of USD supply in the domestic FX market. However, the sequential deceleration in inflows warrants attention — if this trend continues into Q3, it could reduce a key pillar of peso support at a time when geopolitical uncertainty (US-Iran) and Asian FX volatility are already applying downward pressure. For PSEi and PGB investors, the data confirms that foreign appetite for Philippine assets has not reversed materially, despite lingering global market volatility. Key forward-looking question: whether July and August data will reflect any acceleration driven by the BSP's anticipated terminal rate signal, or whether risk-off conditions drive a reversal into net outflows. This data series will be essential for assessing balance of payments dynamics and BSP's reserve management posture.

medium.title: BPI Expects Profit Rebound This Semester
medium.summary:
Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI), one of the Philippines' largest listed banks and a significant PSEi component, expects second-half profit growth to outperform the first half, underpinned by continued expansion of its corporate loan book. Management flagged headwinds in consumer and SME lending segments, suggesting a degree of credit stress at the retail level that bears monitoring. For equity investors with PSEi exposure, BPI's guidance is a positive near-term signal for the banking sub-index, though the bifurcation between corporate and retail lending performance warrants attention as an indicator of broader household financial health. This earnings trajectory also has implications for credit growth data, which BSP monitors closely in its monetary policy deliberations.

---

medium.title: World Bank Keeps 2026 Philippine Growth Forecast Unchanged
medium.summary: The World Bank maintained its 2026 Philippine GDP growth forecast at 3.7% — within the government's 3.5%–4.5% target — but trimmed its 2027 projection to 5.2% from 5.6% previously, citing persistent external risks expected to weigh on economic activity into next year. The downward revision for 2027 signals that global headwinds, likely including trade uncertainty and tighter financial conditions, are expected to have a lagged drag on the Philippine economy. For bond and FX investors, a stable but modestly subdued growth outlook reduces the urgency for aggressive BSP rate hikes, which could be supportive for Philippine government bonds (PGBs) at the longer end. However, the lowered 2027 forecast may temper foreign investor enthusiasm for PHP assets on a medium-term basis. Watch for BSP's own growth assessment in upcoming Monetary Board meetings for alignment or divergence with the World Bank view.

medium.title: Philippine Manufacturing PMI Hits 5-Month High in July
medium.summary: The S&P Global Philippines Manufacturing PMI rose to 51.8 in July from 50.9 in June, marking the third consecutive month of expansion and the strongest reading since February. Production and new orders grew at their fastest pace since February, suggesting broadening momentum in the manufacturing sector. While PMI data is not a direct driver of PHP or bond markets, a sustained expansion above the 50-threshold supports a positive growth narrative that could attract foreign portfolio inflows into PSEi equities and, indirectly, provide mild PHP support. If manufacturing strength feeds into inflationary pressure on input costs or wages, it could also become a marginal factor in BSP's inflation monitoring. This data point adds to the constructive short-term domestic macro backdrop.

medium.title: DoF Proposes Higher Excise Taxes
medium.summary: The Department of Finance is proposing new and increased excise taxes on sweetened beverages, e-cigarettes, flexible plastics, luxury vehicles, and private aircraft as part of its PROGRESS bill, designed to offset revenue losses from proposed personal income tax cuts. The fiscal balancing act is relevant for sovereign bond investors: if passed, the measures could help preserve revenue adequacy and keep the fiscal deficit in check, which would be supportive of Philippine government bond creditworthiness and limit upward pressure on PGB yields from sovereign risk repricing. However, the net impact on inflation — particularly from excise taxes on consumer goods — warrants monitoring, as any inflationary pass-through could complicate BSP's rate-cutting cycle. Bond traders should track legislative progress and DoF revenue projections closely.

medium.title: Philippine Stocks End Higher on Peace Talks and Strong Data
medium.summary: The PSEi gained 1.57% (+98.28 points) to close at 6,334.72, with the broader All Shares Index rising 1.03% to 3,430.16, driven by easing Middle East geopolitical tensions and positive manufacturing activity data. Declining global oil prices following U.S. President Trump's comments on de-escalation reduced cost-push inflation concerns, improving risk appetite for Philippine equities. For fund managers, the rebound signals renewed near-term bullish momentum in the PSEi, though the index remains sensitive to global macro developments. The confluence of easing geopolitical risk and improving domestic PMI data (see below) provides a supportive backdrop for equities; however, investors should monitor whether the Q2 GDP growth slowdown (Article 1) caps the upside.

medium.title: Philippines Manufacturing PMI Expands for a Third Straight Month in July
medium.summary: The S&P Global Philippines Manufacturing PMI rose to 51.8 in July from 50.9 in June, marking a third consecutive month of expansion above the 50-threshold and signaling broadening improvement in operating conditions. Stronger demand drove the expansion, though rising input costs remain a watchpoint for inflation dynamics and BSP policy. For FX and bond traders, sustained manufacturing expansion suggests the Philippine economic backdrop is more resilient than Q2 GDP headline figures imply, which could moderate expectations for aggressive BSP rate cuts. Rising input cost pressures, however, warrant monitoring as a potential inflation re-acceleration risk that could steepen the short end of the yield curve.

medium.title: Weak Consumption and Public Spending Likely Weighed on Q2 GDP Growth
medium.summary: Deutsche Bank Research forecasts Philippine Q2 2026 GDP growth at just 2.5%, while BMI (Fitch Solutions) projects 2.7% — both sharply below the 5.4% expansion recorded in Q2 2025 and below Q1 2026's 2.8%, marking a potential fourth consecutive quarter of deceleration. The primary drags cited are tepid private consumption and weak government spending. For PHP and bond market participants, a significant growth miss would reinforce the case for further BSP monetary easing, which is bullish for duration but could exert modest downside pressure on the peso if it amplifies risk-off sentiment toward Philippine assets. The official Q2 GDP print will be a key near-term catalyst — investors should position accordingly ahead of the release.

medium.title: Philippine exports seen resilient despite 12.5% US tariff
medium.summary:
Analysts expect Philippine merchandise exports to remain broadly resilient under the US's 12.5% tariff regime, supported by exemptions for key export categories including semiconductors, electronics, and select agricultural goods — which together form the backbone of Philippine export revenues. However, labour-intensive sectors such as garments and leather goods face meaningful competitiveness erosion, with associated job loss risks. From a macro and FX standpoint, the resilience of electronics exports is critical to maintaining a healthy trade account and supporting USD inflows, which underpin the peso. Any deterioration in the trade balance — particularly if non-exempt sectors shrink faster than expected — could widen the current account deficit and add structural downward pressure on the PHP. Investors in PHP and PGBs should monitor monthly trade data closely for signs of export volume erosion, as a deteriorating trade position could complicate the BSP's FX management strategy.

---

medium.title: PSEi Falls to 6,200 Range as Traders Lock in Gains
medium.summary: The PSEi declined 0.60% or 38.08 points to close at 6,296.64, while the broader All Shares index also shed 0.43% to finish at 3,415.35. The pullback was driven by profit-taking following the market's sharp rally in the prior session, with cautious sentiment further weighing on sentiment amid ongoing uncertainty surrounding US-Iran peace negotiations. The geopolitical overhang suggests foreign portfolio investors may maintain a defensive posture in the near term, which could translate into mild net selling pressure on Philippine equities and modest headwinds for the PHP via reduced equity-related capital inflows. Fund managers should watch whether the 6,200–6,300 support band holds; a sustained breach could amplify risk-off flows out of local assets.

medium.title: World Bank Says Philippines Needs to Widen Tax Base
medium.summary: The World Bank urged the Philippine government to broaden its tax base, specifically highlighting proposals to expand excise tax coverage as a fiscally sound approach that avoids disproportionately burdening low-to-middle income households. While primarily a fiscal policy story, this is of medium relevance to bond and FX investors: successful tax base widening would improve the government's revenue profile, potentially reducing the fiscal deficit and lowering the government's borrowing requirement. A narrower borrowing program would be constructive for Philippine government bond (PGS) yields and reduce sovereign credit risk — a modest positive signal for PHP stability over the medium term. Investors should monitor legislative progress on the proposed excise tax reforms.
